solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annie perhaps is calm after revision, impressing head of university

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so one piece is set inside the other
after revision says the letters of is calm have been reworked into a new order
head of picks out the first letter of the word university

explanation.surface: A girl called Annie keeps her cool after revising, and makes an impression on the head of the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revision' rearranges IS CALM to MSICAL, and 'impressing' sets U inside it after the M. Annie is a famous stage show, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a well-known stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: ELO finally played my special tune

indicators.note: special suggests something unusual or altered, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of the word played

explanation.surface: The band ELO at last performed a song specially for me.
explanation.walkthrough: ELO (Electric Light Orchestra) is a British rock band. 'finally' gives D; 'special' rearranges ELO, D and MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a sequence of musical notes, a synonym for a melodic line.

clue.text: Sun catches gastropods

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday or the sun
to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper exposes some slugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are molluscs of the class Gastropoda, an example of the group.

clue.text: Tories cage working classes

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over or reshaped, so the letters of Tories cage are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservatives lock up the working classes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are the UK Conservative Party. 'working' pretends to join 'classes' as 'working classes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes are groups or kinds, a synonym for divisions in a classification.

clue.text: Dangerous situation with no power for illumination

indicators.note: with no says that letter is removed from the word for the situation

parts.note: a plight is a dangerous or difficult situation
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A risky position with the electricity cut so there are no lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes P from PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Light is a synonym for illumination, brightness that lets us see.

clue.text: Demanded medical reforms

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters of medical are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone insisted that the health system be overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun about health policy, but it is the verb that rearranges MEDICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have claimed something is to have demanded it as one's right; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Party member commits to change without United Nations

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
to change says the letters of commits are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party member resolves to reform without help from the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'to change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A communist is a member of the Communist Party, an example of a party member.

clue.text: Local turns up with one on horse

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the other piece

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: a local is a British pub, and a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A man from the neighbourhood appears with someone riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub. 'turns up' reverses BAR to RAB, and 'on' puts A above it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse known for speed and endurance, an example of horse.

clue.text: Tinny crushing tall mice

indicators.note: crushing means squashing out of shape, so the letters of tall mice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tin is squashing some big mice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinny describes a thin metal sound or quality, synonymous with metal-like.

clue.text: Coming to a conclusion, partly, inside CID in Gloucester

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Police detectives in Gloucester are reaching a verdict on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police; Gloucester is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciding means reaching a judgment, a synonym for settling a question.

clue.text: Smallest one ultimately comes in after all the others

indicators.note: comes in says that the single letter enters the longer piece

parts.note: coming after all the others means being final in order

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: The smallest runner finishes behind everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E from 'one', and 'comes in' puts it inside LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, a synonym for smallest in amount or size.

clue.text: Type of move a man might do on a horse?

definitions.text: Type of move a man might do on a horse?

parts.words: Type of move a man might do on a horse?
parts.note: the horse is not an animal but the vaulting horse in a gym, so the move is a vault or similar exercise

explanation.surface: What sort of manoeuvre might a rider perform on horseback?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests riding; the horse is the padded vaulting apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an exercise routine performed on gym apparatus such as the vaulting horse.

clue.text: Engaging sidelight fully or partially?

indicators.note: partially says only part of the words sidelight fully is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A question of whether a car's side lamp is charming in whole or in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link; 'partially' signals the run of letters across sidelight fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming or pleasing, a synonym for something that gives great pleasure.

clue.text: Female went first and escaped

parts.note: to have gone first is to have led

explanation.surface: A woman took the lead and got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled is the past tense of flee, a synonym for having escaped.

clue.text: Unfortunately I've sat with four people unduly preferred by the Queen?

definitions.text: people unduly preferred by the Queen?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of I've sat and four are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone regrets sitting with four courtiers the monarch liked too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal favourites were courtiers given excessive preference by a monarch, as the question hints.

clue.text: Company talk about fantastic gains

indicators.note: about says the speech goes round the other piece

parts.note: an oration is a formal talk or speech

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and changed, so the letters of gains are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm's spokesman discusses its remarkable profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a guest or companion, but here it means a business body.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a business organisation; the words are synonyms for a body of people.

clue.text: Swearing awfully about new meeting

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of Swearing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cursing terribly about a new meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns SWEARING into ASWERING, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering a need means meeting it, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Come with coin for a change — it's cheap

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of Come and coin are mixed up

explanation.surface: Bring some money for once, as it is inexpensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean cheap or good value, as in an economic price.

clue.text: That's all there is, everyone

definitions.meaning: the whole population or body of people, everybody under consideration

explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything in existence, and by extension the whole population considered.

clue.text: A time to get involved in rugby score discussion

indicators.note: getting involved in means going inside, so these letters are placed within the score

parts.note: a conversion is the kick after a try in rugby, worth two points

explanation.surface: A moment to join in a chat about the points in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: A conversion is the extra kick at goal after a try in rugby, so 'rugby score' is fair even to readers who don't follow the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion is a talk between people, a synonym for an exchange of views.

clue.text: At first, Calvin Klein designed for money

indicators.note: designed means made to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged
at first picks out the opening letter of the word Calvin

explanation.surface: Calvin Klein originally created clothes to make cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvin Klein is a US fashion designer. 'At first' gives C, and 'designed' rearranges C plus KLEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is a US five-cent coin, an example of money.

clue.text: Information held by a Cyprus bureau

indicators.note: held by means contained, so the information word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Intelligence kept by a Cypriot office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is a container signal: the slang word for information sits inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an office or bureau providing a particular service; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Vehicle returns with last of many sailors

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word for the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a type of vehicle

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word many

explanation.surface: A truck comes back with the final passengers of a crowd of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns VAN into NAV.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is a country's sea force, collectively its sailors.

clue.text: Rendering half of period building

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters of period

parts.note: building in the sense of shaping or making means forming

explanation.surface: Applying plaster to a historic structure from a past era.
explanation.walkthrough: Rendering here means performing a piece of music or a role, not plastering a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering a song or part means giving a performance of it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Set of competitors and I fled ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of I fled are rearranged

explanation.surface: Faced with a set of rivals, I ran from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for a sports ground, but it is the past tense of grind, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The field in a race or contest means all the entrants taking part.

clue.text: One might call it a levy on independence

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the other piece

parts.note: a levy is a tax
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A tax charged on being independent.
explanation.walkthrough: You call a cab, and 'on' puts TAX above I in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is something people call or hail, which this cryptic description captures.

clue.text: Horse eating processed grain that's often spread

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the horse word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: processed means treated or changed, so the letters of grain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mare tucks into some refined cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' is the anagram signal and 'eating' the container; the definition is the descriptive phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter substitute is commonly spread on bread, so the description fits.

clue.text: Stolen — thanks man!

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a thing has been nicked, thanking a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stolen has been taken without permission; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: After church J.R. perhaps is meditating

parts.note: J.R. Ewing was the scheming oil baron in the US soap Dallas, an example of a member of that family

explanation.surface: J.R. is deep in thought after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places CH first in a normal charade order. J.R. Ewing was the villain of the 1980s American TV soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing something over means pondering it, a synonym for meditating on it.

clue.text: Model transforms lips within 24 hours

indicators.note: within says the rearranged letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours

indicators.note: transforms means changes the shape of, so the letters of lips are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion model has her lips altered in a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is a verb here: to model clothes is to show them off; 'transforms' signals the anagram and 'within' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To model clothes is to show them off, a synonym for exhibiting them.
